title: Franciscans today
hook: friars in cities, soup kitchens and missions

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Transitus: Francis on the bare ground, singing a psalm, greeting death as family. Your line was welcome, sister death. How did that last breath of the night feel? Day one thousand two hundred twenty-seven.

Before sunrise in a big city, a line is already forming outside a side door. Men with backpacks, a mother with a stroller, an old man in a coat too heavy for the weather. The door opens, and the person holding it is a friar. Down the street, another one is hearing confessions in a downtown church at lunchtime. Across an ocean, another is teaching in a village school, or sitting with the sick in a clinic. Francis died on the bare ground in Assisi. His brothers never stopped walking. Today, where you might find them now.
screen: `A LINE BEFORE SUNRISE.` → `A FRIAR HOLDS THE DOOR.` →`HIS BROTHERS NEVER STOPPED.`

segments.voice: Francis didn't found a monastery on a hilltop. He sent his brothers out. His Rule pictures them going through the world, owning nothing, working with their hands, and taking what they need as poor men do. So the friars ended up where people are: in towns, then cities. That's still the shape today. The family of Francis now has several branches of friars, among them the Friars Minor, the Conventuals, and the Capuchins we met a few days ago. There are the Poor Clares behind their grilles, praying for the world. There are communities of Franciscan sisters running schools and hospitals. And there are lay Franciscans, married people with jobs and kids, who follow Francis in ordinary life. What do they do? Ordinary things, done close to the poor. A soup kitchen. A shelter. A parish on a block nobody else wanted. A chaplain at a prison or a hospital. A mission far from home. Jesus's words in Matthew could be painted over the door, in the Douay-Rheims: "For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in." One more thing, because it gets quoted on Franciscan walls too. Francis is often said to have told people to preach the Gospel always and use words only if necessary. The early sources don't record him saying it. What his early Rule does say is close: that all the brothers should preach by their deeds. The friar holding that side door before sunrise is doing exactly that.
screen: `NOT A HILLTOP, BUT THE ROAD.` · `FRIARS, CLARES, SISTERS, LAY FOLLOWERS.` · `SOUP KITCHENS, PRISONS, MISSIONS.` · `PREACH BY YOUR DEEDS.` · then, large: `I WAS A STRANGER, AND YOU TOOK ME IN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give to a Franciscan work. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one place near you that feeds people, shelters them or sits with them when they're sick. It might be run by friars or sisters, or by someone else entirely. Picture its door, and the line outside it. Then choose one small gift you can give today: a few dollars, a bag of groceries, an hour of your time, or simply finding out where it is. If you pray, you can pray for the people in that line and the people holding the door. The bell holds the time.
Franciscans today. Friars, sisters, Poor Clares and lay followers of Francis, still close to the poor, in cities, kitchens and missions. Today's word.
Your line: still walking. Today, carry out the gift you chose, even a small one, and let it preach without a word. Day one thousand two hundred twenty-seven.

screen: `DAY 1227 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A FRANCISCAN DAY AT HOME.`

howItsDone: Franciscan friars and sisters serve in parishes, soup kitchens, shelters, schools, hospitals and missions, and Catholics often support their works with gifts of money, food or time.

original.note: Latin: the Order of Friars Minor, the lesser brothers. it's why friars sign their names with OFM.

trapdoor: what you thought: Franciscans were a medieval thing, monks in old paintings.
what it means: friars, sisters and lay followers still serving close to the poor, in cities, kitchens and missions.
what a scholar hears: the initials after a friar's name tell his branch: OFM for the Friars Minor, OFM Conv. for the Conventuals, OFM Cap. for the Capuchins.

notes: The saying 'preach the Gospel at all times; when necessary, use words' is not found in the early Franciscan sources; the Earlier Rule (ch. 17) says all the brothers should preach by their works. Confirm.
